page: Vultr vbm-128c-2048gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server in the Bare Metal SSD family, designed for high-density compute and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the machine is driven by AMD EPYC 7713 processors featuring 128 physical cores, 256 vCPUs via two threads per core, and a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing execution free from virtualization overhead.

The hardware platform is configured with 2048.0 GB of system memory, providing a generous allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local primary storage is supplied by a 960 GB SSD, and network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server integrates no GPU hardware, dedicating all system resources entirely to central processing and large memory transactions.

A notable configuration tradeoff is the moderate local storage capacity of 960 GB alongside an expansive 2 TB RAM footprint. Workloads requiring extreme disk-bound persistence may necessitate network storage additions. The server is primarily suitable for large in-memory databases, dense bare-metal hypervisor deployments, enterprise resource planning platforms, and intensive distributed analytics.
